messages.author: 1ecb0a398ebb03f9
messages.subject: GSoC 2020: Coding Period Begins!
parts:
Hello all, 

Hope you all had great time getting familiar to R Community past month, and now have bonded with Mentors of your projects. 

We just wanted to wish you good luck for the coding phase that began from 1st June. Remember phase 1 evaluation begins from June 29, if you are facing any issues with project or the proposal or have come across new issues or bugs that require you to take more time then expected, please discuss it with your mentors forehand, so that they can take it into consideration when evaluating your Phase 1 submissions. 

Few Important things to keep in mind: 

1. If you fail to submit your phase 1 report/commits in time, mentors will have no choice but to fail you and you will be removed from the program. 

2. If mentors feel you have not committed appropriate time [as per gsoc guidelines and as per mentors suggestions] to the program or project or haven't contributed enough over the period, you could fail in phase 1 or future evaluations at their discretion. 

3. We will also encourage GSoC Students to write article or blog sharing their experience and code with other community members and world, though this was more ideal during community bonding period, but this would also be taken into account in respect to your active engagement with the R community. We all would love to know about your projects and journey so far. 

4. Mentors: Please assign or discuss internally which mentors [or as mentioned in wiki] will be evaluating the students, we don't want them to face any issues regarding this, as without your evaluation, they won't be able to move to phase 2. 

For any issues or discuss, please reach out to me, Toby, Brian or Vijay. 

Or ping us at our slack channel. 

Happy Coding or Happy Mentoring.

Thanks,
Vivek

messages.author: c9416b6005bf4eb7
messages.subject: Re: GSoC 2020: Coding Period Begins!
parts:
Hi Vivek thanks for the update / reminders.

About point (4) we absolutely need 100% mentor evals this summer. Google takes evals very seriously, and R project will be severely penalized if ANY of the mentor evals are missing. For example, if any evals are missing, R may be reject from participating in GSOC in future years. To enforce this, we required an EVALUATING MENTOR for each student project. That mentor (as mentioned in the student project proposal / wiki page) is responsible for submitting the eval. Other mentors are responsible for reminding the EVALUATING MENTOR to submit the eval. Any mentors of students with missing evals this summer will be penalized by not being able to participate in future edition(s) of R-GSOC.

Also this might be used by Google to severely penalize our organization in coming years in terms of number of slots or even may be rejected in selection process on these grounds.  To enforce this, we required an EVALUATING MENTOR for each student project. That mentor (as mentioned in the student project proposal / wiki page) is responsible for submitting the eval.  

For any issues or concerns, please reach out to me, Toby, Brian, Narayani or Vijay.
